# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
alpha = -loc*(open/close)**5  # long closes near the low, scaled by the open-to-close drop

# Thesis: High prices that coincide with high volume rank are exhausted. (Alpha #44, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
alpha = -ts_corr_binary(high, cs_rank(volume), 5)  # negative 5-day corr of high and volume rank

# Thesis: Persistent co-movement of volume and VWAP ranks marks crowded trades. (Alpha #50, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
c = ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(volume), cs_rank(vwap_last_hour), 5)  # 5-day corr of volume rank and VWAP rank
alpha = -ts_max(cs_rank(c), 5)  # short the most persistent co-movers

# Thesis: A change in where the close sits within the day's range reverts. (Alpha #53, adapted)
# Note: Slow re-run requested by Abhinav after a strong Fast screen.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991
pos = ((close - low) - (high - close))/(close - low + 0.001*close)  # close location within the day's range
alpha = -delta(pos, 10)  # fade the 10-day change in close location

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term reversal, to cut turnover and pool correlation.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_054 Fast IR .111, TVR 1.38, Fast pool corr .993.
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
r = cs_zscore(-loc*(open/close)**5)  # Alpha #54: long closes near the low after a drop
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996), the partner behind 3 of our submissions
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # reversal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term reversal, to cut turnover and pool correlation.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: 5-day smoothing. Parent A101_054 Fast IR .111, TVR 1.38, Fast pool corr .993.
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
r = cs_zscore(ts_mean(-loc*(open/close)**5, 5))  # 5-day average of the Alpha #54 signal (lower turnover)
alpha = r  # smoothed contrarian signal

# Thesis: A close near the low on a gap-down open rebounds (delay-0 contrarian). (Alpha #54, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term reversal, to cut turnover and pool correlation.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: 5-day smoothing + accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_054 Fast IR .111, TVR 1.38, Fast pool corr .993.
loc = (low - close)/(low - high - 0.001*close)  # how far the close sits above the low, 0..1
r = cs_zscore(ts_mean(-loc*(open/close)**5, 5))  # 5-day average of the Alpha #54 signal
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996), the partner behind 3 of our submissions
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # smoothed reversal + accruals at 1.5x
